device.model: Low Noise Rubidium GNSDO (PRE), GPS/GNSS-disciplined rubidium oscillator
device.name: Jackson Labs Low Noise Rubidium GNSDO

facts.text: The upstream repository is a Linux serial-port simulator of the SCPI behaviour of a Low Noise Rubidium GNSDO, a GPS/GNSS-disciplined rubidium time-frequency reference; it is not a client library.
The serial port is 8N1 at 115200 baud
A client writes a command line ending in CRLF (the README shows b'*IDN?\r\n')
The simulator writes a response followed by CRLF
Command matching is case-insensitive: normalize_command strips the line ends and returns text.upper()
A command with a value is split at the first space into a command prefix and its value
The identity reply is 'Jackson Labs, LN Rb GPSDO (PRE), Firmware Rev <firmware>'
SYNC:LOCKED? answers '1' when the oscillator is locked and '0' when it is not
SYNC:TINT? is the time interval error in seconds, printed in scientific notation
SYNC:HEALTH? is a hexadecimal bit mask: 0x4 is a TINT above 210 ns, 0x8 a runtime below 200 s, 0x10 a holdover above 60 s and 0x400 a hardware fault
SYNC:HOLD:INIT sets holdover, clears the lock and records the holdover start; SYNC:HOLD:REC:INIT clears holdover, restores the lock and clears the start
SYNC:SOUR:MODE <value> stores any non-empty value as the synchronization source mode
SYNC:HOLD:DUR? answers two comma-separated numbers: the holdover duration in seconds and 1 while in holdover or 0 otherwise
GPS:SAT:TRAC:COUN? and GPS:SAT:VIS:COUN? answer the tracked and visible satellite counts
MEAS:TEMP? returns the PCB temperature
MEAS:VOLT? returns the TCXO adjustment voltage, not the power-supply voltage; the comment gives about 1.6 to 1.7 V from a real device output
MEAS:POW? returns the power-supply input voltage; the comment gives about 11.7 to 11.74 V from a real device output
CSAC:STATUS? answers 0 when the atomic clock module is healthy and 1 when it is not
CSAC:TEMP?, CSAC:SN? and CSAC:LIFE? answer the module temperature, serial number and lifetime hours
PTIME:OUTPUT? answers 1 or 0, while the PTIME:OUTPUT setter accepts ON or OFF
PTIME:LEAP:ACC? answers the accumulated GPS-UTC leap seconds
DIAG:LIFE:COUN? answers the lifetime in hours, increased by the simulator's runtime
The simulator considers the oscillator locked only when at least four satellites are tracked
The GPS survey variance limit is 150000 in the simulator state
The atomic-lock warmup time is 120 s, from the manual's 'less than 2 minutes warmup time to atomic lock' comment
